<!-- PR title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] muse-spark: TF32 cluster split-K GEMM for the decode router logits -->

**Depends on #47561** (this PR is one commit on top of it; review the last commit).

## Motivation

With #47517 (and #47561 on SM107) the router stream finishes last at most decode sizes, so the router GEMM gates when the experts start. This PR:

1. Adds a fused split-K router GEMM (CuTe DSL, TF32): K is split across a thread-block cluster and the partial sums are reduced in distributed shared memory, in one launch instead of cuBLAS's GEMM + reduce. A per-GPU tactic table (SM103, SM107) picks the tactic per token count; ranges without a winning tactic keep cuBLAS.
2. Re-tunes #47561's split thresholds on top of it: GB300 now takes the split from M = 512 (where the main stream gates again); SM107 keeps it from M = 8.

## Modifications

- `muse_spark_router_gemm_cutedsl.py` (new): the TF32 cluster split-K GEMM (`router_tf32`), its tactic validation, and `_SERVE_TABLES`, the serving tactic per (compute capability, token range). `router_tf32_eligible` is true only where the table has a tactic (2 <= M <= 1024) and TF32 matmuls are allowed; everything else keeps cuBLAS. The fp32 inputs and the TF32 math are the same as cuBLAS's under `float32_matmul_precision("high")`, which the server sets; only the split-K reduction order differs. Under `"highest"` the kernel is never taken, so the logits stay FP32.
- `muse_spark.py`: `MuseSpark1xRouter` calls `router_tf32` when eligible (the table has a tactic for this GPU and token count), after the existing GEMV path. There is no switch: GPUs or token counts without a tactic keep cuBLAS.
- `routed_moe_split.py` (#47561): GB300 takes the routing-metadata split from M = 512 at TP4 and TP8. With this PR's router the main stream trails the router stream by 3.2-4.7 µs from M = 512, which the split recovers (2.8-4.7 µs per layer; neutral at TP8 M = 1024); below M = 512 the main stream trails by at most 1.6 µs or the router still gates, so GB300 keeps the fused routing there (see "GB300 split thresholds").

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

The logits keep fp32 inputs and TF32 math; only the split-K summation order differs from cuBLAS, so logits differ in the last bits and the selected experts can change on near ties.

Muse Spark Open, #47517 + #47561, router GEMM off vs on, DFlash (real acceptance), sgl-eval with T=1.0, top_p=1.0, top_k=64, xhigh reasoning; GSM8K max 65K tokens, AIME26 30 problems x 16 repeats, max 131K tokens.

| GPU | TP | router GEMM | GSM8K | AIME26 pass@1 | AIME26 pass@16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SM107 | 4 | this PR | 97.80% | 96.46% | 100% |
| SM107 | 8 | this PR | 97.65% | 95.21% | 100% |

GB300, TP4 unless noted, same sgl-eval settings:

| tree | GSM8K | AIME26 pass@1 | AIME26 pass@16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main + #47561 + this PR | 97.35% | 96.04% | 100% |
| main + #47561 + this PR, TP8 | 97.73% | 95.62% | 100% |

<details>
<summary>Kernel tests</summary>

`test_muse_spark_router_gemm_cutedsl.py`: every serving tactic of this GPU's table at both ends of its token range against an fp64 reference (max error / max logit < 2e-3; measured ~3e-4 over K = 8192) and bitwise reproducible across runs; every M up to 1024 resolves to a valid tactic or to cuBLAS, consistently with `router_tf32_eligible`.

- No M is eligible under `float32_matmul_precision("highest")` (regression test; fails without the precision gate).
- Four explicit tactics (segment shorter than one logits row, split 16 with `cta_k` 128, partial last token tile without PDL, 128-expert tile) run on any SM10x GPU, so B200 CI covers the kernel without a serving table.
- CI: B200 (`base-b-kernel-unit`, explicit tactics) and B300 (`base-c`, SM103 table). No CI runner has SM107; its table is covered by the runs below.

- SM107: 18 / 18 passed; `test_muse_spark_routed_moe_split.py` with the GB300 thresholds: 22 / 22.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

**Setup.** Base = our Muse decode stack with #47517 and #47561, this PR = the same stack + this PR (router GEMM on); FlashInfer autotune off and per-token NVFP4 activation off on both sides.

### Standalone: cuBLAS TF32 vs this PR's GEMM

Router logits `x[M, 8192] fp32 @ W[256, 8192]^T`, CUDA graph of 60 calls with a distinct (cold) weight each, µs per call. Serving tactic = the table's entry, picked beside the main stream rather than alone; fastest alone = the best of every valid tactic (expert tile {64, 128} x token tile x split {2, 4, 8, 16} x K tile {32, 64, 128}). Both paths keep fp32 inputs and TF32 math (max |err| / max |logit| vs fp64 2-3e-4 for both).

| M | GB300 cuBLAS | GB300 serving tactic | speedup | GB300 fastest alone | speedup | SM107 cuBLAS | SM107 serving tactic | speedup | SM107 fastest alone | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 7.49 | 3.20 | 2.34x | 3.02 | 2.48x | 4.70 | 3.61 | 1.30x | 2.19 | 2.15x |
| 16 | 7.55 | 3.50 | 2.15x | 3.13 | 2.41x | 4.73 | 3.64 | 1.30x | 2.27 | 2.09x |
| 32 | 7.72 | 6.04 | 1.28x | 3.37 | 2.29x | 4.52 | 3.66 | 1.23x | 2.48 | 1.83x |
| 64 | 7.77 | 6.05 | 1.28x | 4.00 | 1.94x | 4.69 | 3.18 | 1.47x | 3.05 | 1.54x |
| 128 | 9.32 | 5.31 | 1.76x | 5.30 | 1.76x | 4.86 | 3.73 | 1.31x | 3.73 | 1.31x |
| 256 | 11.04 | 6.83 | 1.62x | 6.83 | 1.62x | 5.84 | cuBLAS | - | 4.60 | 1.27x |
| 512 | 15.95 | 8.84 | 1.80x | 8.28 | 1.93x | 6.65 | 8.26 | 0.81x | 6.46 | 1.03x |
| 1024 | 18.50 | 12.35 | 1.50x | 11.72 | 1.58x | 9.34 | cuBLAS | - | 9.77 | 0.96x |

The fastest tactic alone is a 16-CTA cluster at small M on both GPUs; beside the main stream it waits for SMs, so the serving tables use smaller clusters where that costs more in context than it saves alone. On SM107 the M = 512 serving tactic is slower than cuBLAS alone but ends the router stream earlier in serving (nsys below).

### How the tactics were picked

Same procedure on both GPUs; the tactic that is fastest alone is often not the one that ends the router stream earliest, because a large cluster waits for SMs the main stream holds.

1. Isolated sweep (CUDA graph, 60 calls with a distinct cold weight each): every valid tactic (expert tile {64, 128} x token tile x split {2, 4, 8, 16} x K tile {32, 64, 128}; GB300 also PDL on/off) at M = 8..1024, pruned to the top candidates per M (the standalone table above).
2. In context, at TP4 and TP8: the candidates on the router stream beside the main stream, CUDA graph. GB300: the decode MoE front as served (projection slice -> gather + norm + NVFP4 quant on the main stream; router GEMM -> fused top-8 routing on the router stream), distinct weights per layer, 5 rotated trials; every entry is within 0.5 µs of the best measured tactic at both TP sizes. SM107: a stand-in pooler GEMM beside the router GEMM to prune, then A/B in TP4 / TP8 serving with #47561 (DFlash decode, nsys experts start, median over layers).
3. A token range keeps cuBLAS unless a tactic beat it at both TP sizes.

### SM107: end to end (nsys)

Experts start: µs from the end of the attention boundary (the `o_proj` all-reduce) to the first expert GEMM, device 0, median over layers, then median of three runs per side on the final code. saved = base - this PR. Projected = saved x 60 MoE layers / (62 layers x base layer time). Where the table keeps cuBLAS (c = 32, 128), both sides run the same kernels and the difference is run-to-run noise.

| c | M | router GEMM | TP4 experts start (µs) | TP4 saved | TP4 projected | TP8 experts start (µs) | TP8 saved | TP8 projected |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8 | this PR | 12.7 -> 10.3 | +2.4 | -2.7% | 11.2 -> 8.5 | +2.7 | -3.7% |
| 2 | 16 | this PR | 12.9 -> 9.9 | +3.0 | -3.0% | 11.7 -> 8.7 | +3.0 | -3.6% |
| 4 | 32 | this PR | 11.0 -> 10.3 | +0.7 | -0.6% | 9.6 -> 8.9 | +0.7 | -0.8% |
| 8 | 64 | this PR | 14.3 -> 12.8 | +1.5 | -1.1% | 12.7 -> 12.1 | +0.6 | -0.6% |
| 16 | 128 | this PR | 15.1 -> 15.1 | 0.0 | 0.0% | 13.8 -> 12.8 | +1.0 | -0.8% |
| 32 | 256 | cuBLAS | 17.9 -> 17.7 (same kernels) | - | - | 15.5 -> 15.5 (same kernels) | - | - |
| 64 | 512 | this PR | 21.5 -> 19.4 | +2.1 | -0.8% | 18.9 -> 17.2 | +1.7 | -0.8% |
| 128 | 1024 | cuBLAS | 29.0 -> 28.5 (same kernels) | - | - | 41.3 -> 39.9 (same kernels) | - | - |

- The router GEMM gates the experts at every concurrency on this base, so its saving shows up one-for-one in when the experts start: 2.4-3.0 µs at c = 1-2.
- At TP4 c = 16 the 16-CTA cluster waits for SMs while the pooler GEMM runs, which absorbs its faster GEMM (9.2 -> 5.2 µs); at TP8 it shows up as -1.0 µs.


### GB300: when the experts' inputs are ready (nsys)

| c | M | TP4 router ready | TP4 gate | TP4 projected | TP8 router ready | TP8 gate | TP8 projected |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8 | 13.34 -> 10.62 | 13.34 -> 12.22 | -0.9% | 12.38 -> 9.95 | 12.38 -> 10.82 | -1.6% |
| 2 | 16 | 13.89 -> 11.30 | 13.89 -> 12.38 | -1.1% | 12.86 -> 10.27 | 12.86 -> 10.94 | -1.8% |
| 4 | 32 | 17.22 -> 14.37 | 17.22 -> 14.37 | -1.6% | 14.24 -> 13.41 | 14.24 -> 13.41 | -0.6% |
| 8 | 64 | 15.84 -> 15.04 | 16.61 -> 16.77 | 0.0% | 15.81 -> 14.66 | 15.81 -> 14.78 | -0.7% |
| 16 | 128 | 23.42 -> 21.12 | 23.42 -> 21.12 | -0.8% | 19.90 -> 17.34 | 19.90 -> 17.60 | -1.2% |
| 32 | 256 | 27.78 -> 25.79 | 27.78 -> 25.79 | -0.6% | 26.91 -> 24.67 | 26.91 -> 24.67 | -0.9% |
| 64 | 512 | 42.56 -> 34.50 | 42.56 -> 38.56 | -0.9% | 39.42 -> 31.14 | 39.42 -> 35.81 | -1.1% |

The router stream is 0.8-8 µs shorter at every point. Where it still gates (TP4 c = 4, 16, 32) the whole saving shows; where the main stream now gates (c >= 64), the remaining slack is what the split recovers.

### GB300 split thresholds (#47561)

With this PR, split off vs on (same tree): the split moves the routing metadata (4-8 µs) off the main stream, so it saves up to how far the main stream trails the router stream, minus its fixed cost (a separate populate launch; GEMM1 waits on a cross-stream event instead of chaining behind the routing with PDL).

| c | M | main trails router by (TP4) | TP4 saved | main trails router by (TP8) | TP8 saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1-32 | 8-256 | <= 1.6 µs, or the router gates | within noise or a loss | <= 0.7 µs, or the router gates | within noise |
| 64 | 512 | 3.8 µs | +3.5 µs | 4.7 µs | +4.7 µs |
| 128 | 1024 | 3.2 µs | +2.8 µs | 3.7 µs | -0.2 µs |

So the split is enabled from M = 512 at TP4 and TP8.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

`muse_spark.py` now imports `muse_spark_router_gemm_cutedsl` at load time, and that module imports `cuda.bindings.driver` and `cutlass` at the top (lines 77-86). Without CuTe DSL, `sglang.srt.models.muse_spark` no longer imports.

**Example**

`test/registered/rl/test_fp32_lm_head.py` runs in AMD CI (`stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd`). On ROCm, `test_logits_buffer_shapes_and_transforms` imports `MuseSpark1xLogitsProcessor` from this file and passes on main today. The ROCm image has no `cutlass` (the same CI log shows `No module named 'cutlass'`), so this test will fail.

**Fix**

Keep `router_tf32_eligible` free of `cutlass` and load the kernel lazily, as `muse_spark_router_gemv_cutedsl.py` does in `_compile` / `_kernel_type`.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

`RouterTactic` is a new `@dataclasses.dataclass`. The repo rule `.claude/rules/no-dataclasses.md` asks new data containers to use `msgspec.Struct`.

**Fix**

Use `class RouterTactic(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True):` with the same fields. A frozen Struct stays hashable, so the `_COMPILE_CACHE` key and the `functools.lru_cache` on `serve_tactic` still work. In `default_tactic`, replace `dataclasses.replace(...)` with `msgspec.structs.replace(...)`.

@@ -0,0 +1,889 @@
+"""Muse Spark router logits on SM10x: TF32 tcgen05 GEMM with a cluster split-K.
+
+Computes ``logits[M, E] = x[M, H] @ W[E, H]^T`` (fp32 in, fp32 accumulate, fp32 out)
+in one launch; cuBLAS's TF32 path runs a split-K GEMM plus a separate reduce kernel.
+
+Both operands are TMA-loaded through a TF32 tensor map,
+so the copy engine rounds them fp32 -> TF32 (round to nearest even) on the way into
+shared memory: the MMA sees exactly the operands of a round-to-nearest TF32 GEMM,
+and the weight is used as stored.
+
+The problem is swapped so the experts fill the MMA M dimension and the few tokens
+sit in N. In kernel coordinates:
+  A:  (E, K, L)  K-major  -- router weight
+  B:  (M, K, L)  K-major  -- activations
+  C:  (E, M, L)  E-major  -- view of the row-major [M, E] logits
+E and K are static (one compile per router shape); M is dynamic; L = 1.
+
+## Grid and clusters
+  grid    = (E / cta_m, token_tiles * split_k, 1), cluster = (1, split_k, 1)
+  The ``split_k`` CTAs of a cluster share one (cta_m, cta_n) output tile and each
+  accumulates an equal, contiguous K slice; the epilogue reduces the slices over
+  DSMEM. Larger M runs several token tiles (grid-y = token tile * split_k + rank).
+  There is no TMA multicast: each CTA loads its own K slice.
+
+## Warp specialization (8 warps, 256 threads/CTA)
+  Warps 0-3  EPILOG  TMEM alloc/free; TMEM -> RMEM, split-K reduce-scatter over
+                     DSMEM, st.global
+  Warp 4     MMA     tcgen05.mma into TMEM; releases each stage (tcgen05.commit)
+  Warp 5     LOAD_W  TMA-loads weight tiles into sA[..., stage]; with PDL it does
+                     not wait for the previous kernel and launches the dependent
+                     grid once its loads are issued
+  Warp 6     LOAD_X  griddepcontrol.wait (PDL), then TMA-loads activation tiles
+                     into sB[..., stage]
+  Warp 7     idle
+
+## Synchronization
+  full[stage]       2 arrivals (LOAD_W + LOAD_X arrive_and_expect_tx) + TMA bytes
+  empty[stage]      1 arrival (MMA tcgen05.commit)
+  acc pipeline      PipelineUmmaAsync, 1 stage: MMA -> EPILOG ("accumulator ready")
+  tmem barrier      named barrier (MMA + EPILOG) for retrieving the TMEM pointer
+  mbar_reduce       1 arrival (EPILOG thread 0 arrive_and_expect_tx) + the
+                    (S - 1) * SEG * 4 bytes the peers st.async into sSlots
+  All mbarriers are initialized before the cluster arrive/wait, so no peer can
+  credit mbar_reduce before it exists.
+
+## Split-K reduce-scatter epilogue
+  Rank g of the cluster owns segment g of the output tile: SEG = cta_m * cta_n / S
+  floats, i.e. whole token rows (or part of one row for small tiles).
+    1. registers -> sStage (cta_m x cta_n, token rows), one st.shared.f32 per
+       register; 16 B chunks XOR-swizzled per row (column ^ 4 * (row % 8)), so
+       every 8-thread phase of an ld.shared.v4.f32 and 16-thread phase of an
+       ld.shared.v2.f32 hits 8 distinct 16 B chunks; named barrier;
+    2. every thread copies 16 B pieces of the other ranks' segments:
+       ld.shared.v4.f32 from sStage -> st.async.v4 into the owner's
+       sSlots[:, slot];
+    3. owner: wait for the peer bytes; each thread takes 2 consecutive floats of
+       its segment: ld.shared.v2.f32 of its own sStage + (S - 1) of sSlots in
+       rank order, packed f32x2 adds, st.global.v2.f32 -> each warp writes 256
+       contiguous bytes of one logits row.
+  The summation order is fixed (own partial, then peers in rank order), so the
+  result is deterministic.
+
+## Tile shapes (any tactic, S = split_k)
+  Mma instruction:  Mma_M = cta_m (64 or 128), Mma_N = cta_n, Mma_K = 8 (TF32);
+                    cta_k / 8 MMAs per stage, K / cta_k / S K tiles per rank
+  tcgen05.ld:       16dp256b (32dp32b for cta_m = 128); cta_m * cta_n / 128 fp32
+                    per epilogue thread
+  SMEM:             (cta_m + cta_n) * cta_k * 4 B per stage; sStage cta_m * cta_n * 4 B,
+                    sSlots (S - 1) / S of sStage
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import dataclasses
+import functools
+
+import cuda.bindings.driver as cuda
+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+import cutlass.pipeline as pipeline
+import cutlass.utils as utils
+import torch
+from cutlass import Float32, Int32
+from cutlass.cute.nvgpu import cpasync, tcgen05
+from cutlass.cute.runtime import from_dlpack
+from cutlass.pipeline import pipeline_init_arrive, pipeline_init_wait
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import is_arch_support_pdl
+
+# Tactic space. cta_m = experts per CTA, cta_n = tokens per CTA, split_k = cluster
+# size along K (16 is the non-portable cluster maximum), cta_k = K per pipeline stage.
+_MMA_M = (64, 128)
+_MMA_N = (8, 16, 32, 64, 128)
+_SPLIT_K = (2, 4, 8, 16)
+_CTA_K = (32, 64, 128)
+# Pipeline depth: as deep as shared memory allows, capped at _MAX_STAGES by default;
+# the SM107 serve table raises the cap (_SM107_STAGES) so shared memory binds there too.
+_MIN_STAGES = 2
+_MAX_STAGES = 12
+
+_FP32_BYTES = 4
+_AB_BUFFER_ALIGN_BYTES = 1024  # 128 B swizzle atoms of sA / sB
+_MAILBOX_ALIGN_BYTES = 128
+_MBARRIER_BYTES = 8
+
+_EPILOG_THREADS = 128
+_EPILOG_SYNC_BAR_ID = 1  # staging tile
+_TMEM_ALLOC_SYNC_BAR_ID = 2
+
+_COMPILE_CACHE: dict = {}
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)

@@ -0,0 +1,889 @@
+"""Muse Spark router logits on SM10x: TF32 tcgen05 GEMM with a cluster split-K.
+
+Computes ``logits[M, E] = x[M, H] @ W[E, H]^T`` (fp32 in, fp32 accumulate, fp32 out)
+in one launch; cuBLAS's TF32 path runs a split-K GEMM plus a separate reduce kernel.
+
+Both operands are TMA-loaded through a TF32 tensor map,
+so the copy engine rounds them fp32 -> TF32 (round to nearest even) on the way into
+shared memory: the MMA sees exactly the operands of a round-to-nearest TF32 GEMM,
+and the weight is used as stored.
+
+The problem is swapped so the experts fill the MMA M dimension and the few tokens
+sit in N. In kernel coordinates:
+  A:  (E, K, L)  K-major  -- router weight
+  B:  (M, K, L)  K-major  -- activations
+  C:  (E, M, L)  E-major  -- view of the row-major [M, E] logits
+E and K are static (one compile per router shape); M is dynamic; L = 1.
+
+## Grid and clusters
+  grid    = (E / cta_m, token_tiles * split_k, 1), cluster = (1, split_k, 1)
+  The ``split_k`` CTAs of a cluster share one (cta_m, cta_n) output tile and each
+  accumulates an equal, contiguous K slice; the epilogue reduces the slices over
+  DSMEM. Larger M runs several token tiles (grid-y = token tile * split_k + rank).
+  There is no TMA multicast: each CTA loads its own K slice.
+
+## Warp specialization (8 warps, 256 threads/CTA)
+  Warps 0-3  EPILOG  TMEM alloc/free; TMEM -> RMEM, split-K reduce-scatter over
+                     DSMEM, st.global
+  Warp 4     MMA     tcgen05.mma into TMEM; releases each stage (tcgen05.commit)
+  Warp 5     LOAD_W  TMA-loads weight tiles into sA[..., stage]; with PDL it does
+                     not wait for the previous kernel and launches the dependent
+                     grid once its loads are issued
+  Warp 6     LOAD_X  griddepcontrol.wait (PDL), then TMA-loads activation tiles
+                     into sB[..., stage]
+  Warp 7     idle
+
+## Synchronization
+  full[stage]       2 arrivals (LOAD_W + LOAD_X arrive_and_expect_tx) + TMA bytes
+  empty[stage]      1 arrival (MMA tcgen05.commit)
+  acc pipeline      PipelineUmmaAsync, 1 stage: MMA -> EPILOG ("accumulator ready")
+  tmem barrier      named barrier (MMA + EPILOG) for retrieving the TMEM pointer
+  mbar_reduce       1 arrival (EPILOG thread 0 arrive_and_expect_tx) + the
+                    (S - 1) * SEG * 4 bytes the peers st.async into sSlots
+  All mbarriers are initialized before the cluster arrive/wait, so no peer can
+  credit mbar_reduce before it exists.
+
+## Split-K reduce-scatter epilogue
+  Rank g of the cluster owns segment g of the output tile: SEG = cta_m * cta_n / S
+  floats, i.e. whole token rows (or part of one row for small tiles).
+    1. registers -> sStage (cta_m x cta_n, token rows), one st.shared.f32 per
+       register; 16 B chunks XOR-swizzled per row (column ^ 4 * (row % 8)), so
+       every 8-thread phase of an ld.shared.v4.f32 and 16-thread phase of an
+       ld.shared.v2.f32 hits 8 distinct 16 B chunks; named barrier;
+    2. every thread copies 16 B pieces of the other ranks' segments:
+       ld.shared.v4.f32 from sStage -> st.async.v4 into the owner's
+       sSlots[:, slot];
+    3. owner: wait for the peer bytes; each thread takes 2 consecutive floats of
+       its segment: ld.shared.v2.f32 of its own sStage + (S - 1) of sSlots in
+       rank order, packed f32x2 adds, st.global.v2.f32 -> each warp writes 256
+       contiguous bytes of one logits row.
+  The summation order is fixed (own partial, then peers in rank order), so the
+  result is deterministic.
+
+## Tile shapes (any tactic, S = split_k)
+  Mma instruction:  Mma_M = cta_m (64 or 128), Mma_N = cta_n, Mma_K = 8 (TF32);
+                    cta_k / 8 MMAs per stage, K / cta_k / S K tiles per rank
+  tcgen05.ld:       16dp256b (32dp32b for cta_m = 128); cta_m * cta_n / 128 fp32
+                    per epilogue thread
+  SMEM:             (cta_m + cta_n) * cta_k * 4 B per stage; sStage cta_m * cta_n * 4 B,
+                    sSlots (S - 1) / S of sStage
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import dataclasses
+import functools
+
+import cuda.bindings.driver as cuda
+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+import cutlass.pipeline as pipeline
+import cutlass.utils as utils
+import torch
+from cutlass import Float32, Int32
+from cutlass.cute.nvgpu import cpasync, tcgen05
+from cutlass.cute.runtime import from_dlpack
+from cutlass.pipeline import pipeline_init_arrive, pipeline_init_wait
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import is_arch_support_pdl
+
+# Tactic space. cta_m = experts per CTA, cta_n = tokens per CTA, split_k = cluster
+# size along K (16 is the non-portable cluster maximum), cta_k = K per pipeline stage.
+_MMA_M = (64, 128)
+_MMA_N = (8, 16, 32, 64, 128)
+_SPLIT_K = (2, 4, 8, 16)
+_CTA_K = (32, 64, 128)
+# Pipeline depth: as deep as shared memory allows, capped at _MAX_STAGES by default;
+# the SM107 serve table raises the cap (_SM107_STAGES) so shared memory binds there too.
+_MIN_STAGES = 2
+_MAX_STAGES = 12
+
+_FP32_BYTES = 4
+_AB_BUFFER_ALIGN_BYTES = 1024  # 128 B swizzle atoms of sA / sB
+_MAILBOX_ALIGN_BYTES = 128
+_MBARRIER_BYTES = 8
+
+_EPILOG_THREADS = 128
+_EPILOG_SYNC_BAR_ID = 1  # staging tile
+_TMEM_ALLOC_SYNC_BAR_ID = 2
+
+_COMPILE_CACHE: dict = {}
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class RouterTactic:
+    """One specialization: expert tile, token tile, cluster split-K, stages, K tile."""
+
+    mma_m: int
+    mma_n: int
+    split_k: int
+    ab_stages: int
+    cta_k: int = 64
+    # Programmatic dependent launch (when the device supports it): the weight
+    # loads start before the previous kernel finishes, and the next kernel can
+    # launch as soon as this one has issued its weight loads.
+    pdl: bool = True
+
+
+class RouterGemmKernel:
+    """Router logits: TF32 tcgen05 GEMM, K split over a cluster of ``split_k`` CTAs whose
+    partial tiles are summed by a DSMEM reduce-scatter in the epilogue."""
+
+    def __init__(self, tactic: RouterTactic, use_pdl: bool):
+        self.use_pdl = use_pdl
+        self.acc_dtype = Float32
+        self.mma_tiler = (tactic.mma_m, tactic.mma_n, tactic.cta_k)
+        self.cta_m, self.cta_n, self.cta_k = self.mma_tiler
+        self.num_ab_stage = tactic.ab_stages
+        self.split_k = tactic.split_k
+        self.cta_group = tcgen05.CtaGroup.ONE
+
+        self.epilogue_warp_id = (0, 1, 2, 3)
+        self.mma_warp_id = 4
+        # The weight does not depend on the previous
+        # kernel, the activations do (with PDL only the activation warp waits).
+        self.weight_load_warp_id = 5
+        self.act_load_warp_id = 6
+        # Warp 7 has no role: 8 warps keep the CTA at 256 threads.
+        self.idle_warp_id = 7
+        self.threads_per_cta = 32 * 8
+
+        # Each rank owns 1 / split_k of the output tile (seg floats = whole token
+        # rows) and receives the other ranks' partials of it: its own partial tile
+        # is staged in sStage, the peers' partials of its segment land in sSlots,
+        # and the peers' st.async writes credit exactly the sSlots bytes on the
+        # rank's reduce mbarrier.
+        s = tactic.split_k
+        self.seg = tactic.mma_m * tactic.mma_n // s
+        self.expected_transaction_bytes = (s - 1) * self.seg * _FP32_BYTES
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def __call__(
+        self,
+        w: cute.Tensor,  # (E, K) fp32, static
+        x: cute.Tensor,  # (M, K) fp32, M dynamic
+        out: cute.Tensor,  # (M, E) fp32, M dynamic
+        stream: cuda.CUstream,
+    ):
+        # Kernel views with a unit batch mode: A (E, K, 1), B (M, K, 1), C (E, M, 1).
+        unit = cute.make_layout(1)
+        mA = cute.make_tensor(w.iterator, cute.append(w.layout, unit))
+        mB = cute.make_tensor(x.iterator, cute.append(x.layout, unit))
+        mC = cute.make_tensor(
+            out.iterator, cute.append(cute.select(out.layout, mode=[1, 0]), unit)
+        )
+
+        # TF32 MMA on fp32 operands: Mma_M = cta_m, Mma_N = cta_n, Mma_K = 8.
+        tiled_mma = utils.sm100.make_trivial_tiled_mma(
+            cutlass.TFloat32,
+            utils.LayoutEnum.from_tensor(mA).mma_major_mode(),
+            utils.LayoutEnum.from_tensor(mB).mma_major_mode(),
+            self.acc_dtype,
+            self.cta_group,
+            self.mma_tiler[:2],
+        )
+        # The cluster runs along K only: the TMA and the pipelines see one CTA.
+        cta_layout_vmnk = cute.tiled_divide(
+            cute.make_layout((1, 1, 1)), (tiled_mma.thr_id.shape,)
+        )
+        a_smem_layout_staged = utils.sm100.make_smem_layout_a(
+            tiled_mma, self.mma_tiler, cutlass.TFloat32, self.num_ab_stage
+        )
+        b_smem_layout_staged = utils.sm100.make_smem_layout_b(
+            tiled_mma, self.mma_tiler, cutlass.TFloat32, self.num_ab_stage
+        )
+        a_smem_layout = cute.slice_(a_smem_layout_staged, (None, None, None, 0))
+        b_smem_layout = cute.slice_(b_smem_layout_staged, (None, None, None, 0))
+        tma_op = cpasync.CopyBulkTensorTileG2SOp(self.cta_group)
+        # internal_type=TFloat32: the TMA rounds fp32 -> TF32 on load.
+        tma_atom_a, tma_tensor_a = cute.nvgpu.make_tiled_tma_atom_A(
+            tma_op,
+            mA,
+            a_smem_layout,
+            self.mma_tiler,
+            tiled_mma,
+            cta_layout_vmnk.shape,
+            internal_type=cutlass.TFloat32,
+        )
+        tma_atom_b, tma_tensor_b = cute.nvgpu.make_tiled_tma_atom_B(
+            tma_op,
+            mB,
+            b_smem_layout,
+            self.mma_tiler,
+            tiled_mma,
+            cta_layout_vmnk.shape,
+            internal_type=cutlass.TFloat32,
+        )
+        self.a_load_bytes = cute.size_in_bytes(cutlass.TFloat32, a_smem_layout)
+        self.b_load_bytes = cute.size_in_bytes(cutlass.TFloat32, b_smem_layout)
+
+        acc_shape = tiled_mma.partition_shape_C(self.mma_tiler[:2])
+        tCtAcc_fake = tiled_mma.make_fragment_C(cute.append(acc_shape, 1))
+        self.num_tmem_alloc_cols = utils.get_num_tmem_alloc_cols(tCtAcc_fake)
+
+        self.kernel(
+            tiled_mma,
+            tma_atom_a,
+            tma_tensor_a,
+            tma_atom_b,
+            tma_tensor_b,
+            mC,
+            cta_layout_vmnk,
+            a_smem_layout_staged,
+            b_smem_layout_staged,
+        ).launch(
+            grid=(
+                cute.ceil_div(cute.size(mC, mode=[0]), self.cta_m),
+                cute.ceil_div(cute.size(mC, mode=[1]), self.cta_n) * self.split_k,
+                1,
+            ),
+            block=[self.threads_per_cta, 1, 1],
+            cluster=(1, self.split_k, 1),
+            stream=stream,
+            use_pdl=self.use_pdl,
+        )
+
+    @cute.kernel
+    def kernel(
+        self,
+        tiled_mma: cute.TiledMma,
+        tma_atom_a: cute.CopyAtom,
+        mA_mkl: cute.Tensor,  # (E, K, 1)
+        tma_atom_b: cute.CopyAtom,
+        mB_nkl: cute.Tensor,  # (M, K, 1)
+        mC_mnl: cute.Tensor,  # (E, M, 1)
+        cta_layout_vmnk: cute.Layout,
+        a_smem_layout_staged: cute.ComposedLayout,
+        b_smem_layout_staged: cute.ComposedLayout,
+    ):
+        warp_idx = cute.arch.make_warp_uniform(cute.arch.warp_idx())

+    @cute.jit
+    def load(
+        self,
+        tma_atom: cute.CopyAtom,
+        tXgX: cute.Tensor,  # ((atom_v, rest_v), RestK) of this CTA's tile
+        tXsX: cute.Tensor,  # ((atom_v, rest_v), STAGE)
+        bar_full: cute.Pointer,
+        bar_empty: cute.Pointer,
+        load_bytes: cutlass.Constexpr,
+        k_tile_start: Int32,
+        k_tile_count: cutlass.Constexpr,
+        is_weight: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    ):
+        """One TMA producer: this rank's K tiles of one operand into the stages."""
+        stages = self.num_ab_stage
+        if cutlass.const_expr(self.use_pdl and not is_weight):
+            # The activations come from the previous kernel.
+            cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()
+        # A fresh mbarrier is in phase 0, so waiting on phase 1 passes at once: the
+        # first `stages` tiles go out without waiting for the MMA warp.
+        empty_phase = Int32(1)
+        for k_tile in cutlass.range(k_tile_count, unroll=1):
+            stage = k_tile % stages
+            cute.arch.mbarrier_wait(bar_empty + stage, empty_phase)
+            with cute.arch.elect_one():
+                cute.arch.mbarrier_arrive_and_expect_tx(bar_full + stage, load_bytes)
+            cute.copy(
+                tma_atom,
+                tXgX[(None, k_tile_start + k_tile)],
+                tXsX[(None, stage)],
+                tma_bar_ptr=bar_full + stage,
+            )
+            if stage == stages - 1:
+                empty_phase = empty_phase ^ 1
+        if cutlass.const_expr(self.use_pdl and is_weight):
+            cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()
+        # Keep the CTA alive until the MMA warp has released every stage.
+        for tail in cutlass.range(stages, unroll=1):
+            stage = (tail + k_tile_count) % stages
+            cute.arch.mbarrier_wait(bar_empty + stage, empty_phase)
+            if stage == stages - 1:
+                empty_phase = empty_phase ^ 1

+    @cute.jit
+    def reduce_scatter(
+        self,
+        tTR_rAcc: cute.Tensor,  # fp32 fragment
+        tTR_cC: cute.Tensor,  # (expert, token) coordinates of the fragment
+        mC_mnl: cute.Tensor,  # (E, M, 1)
+        sStage: cute.Tensor,  # (cta_m, cta_n) swizzled: this rank's partial tile
+        sSlots: cute.Tensor,  # (seg, split_k - 1): peers' partials of my segment
+        mbar_reduce: cute.Pointer,
+        epi_tid: Int32,
+        e_idx: Int32,
+        n_idx: Int32,
+        split_rank: Int32,
+    ):
+        RW = self.cta_m  # experts per token row
+        SEG = self.seg
+        S = self.split_k
+        # 4- and 2-float vector views ((V, 1), (rest...)): the swizzle keeps each
+        # 4-expert chunk contiguous, so copies through them are ld.shared.v4 / .v2.
+        sStage4 = cute.zipped_divide(sStage, (4, 1))
+        sStage2 = cute.zipped_divide(sStage, (2, 1))
+        sSlots4 = cute.zipped_divide(sSlots, (4, 1))
+        sSlots2 = cute.zipped_divide(sSlots, (2, 1))
+        r2 = cute.make_rmem_tensor((2,), Float32)
+        r4 = cute.make_rmem_tensor((4,), Float32)
+
+        # 1. Fragment -> sStage (one st.shared.f32 per register).
+        for r in cutlass.range_constexpr(cute.size(tTR_rAcc)):
+            sStage[tTR_cC[r]] = tTR_rAcc[r]
+        pipeline.NamedBarrier(
+            barrier_id=_EPILOG_SYNC_BAR_ID, num_threads=_EPILOG_THREADS
+        ).arrive_and_wait()
+
+        # 2. Send the other ranks' segments, 16 B per st.async: piece j of rank g's
+        #    segment goes to sSlots[4 j : 4 j + 4, slot] of rank g.
+        if epi_tid == 0:
+            cute.arch.mbarrier_arrive_and_expect_tx(
+                mbar_reduce, self.expected_transaction_bytes
+            )
+        n4 = SEG // 4  # 16 B pieces per segment
+        for it in cutlass.range_constexpr(
+            (S * n4 + _EPILOG_THREADS - 1) // _EPILOG_THREADS
+        ):
+            idx = it * _EPILOG_THREADS + epi_tid
+            owner = idx // n4
+            if idx < S * n4 and owner != split_rank:
+                j = idx % n4
+                flat = owner * SEG + 4 * j  # row-major position in the tile
+                cute.autovec_copy(
+                    sStage4[(None, 0), ((flat % RW) // 4, flat // RW)], r4
+                )
+                # Slot of this rank in the owner's sSlots: ranks above the owner
+                # shift down by one (the owner has no slot of its own).
+                slot = split_rank - 1
+                if split_rank < owner:
+                    slot = split_rank
+                # st.async to the owner's sSlots, crediting 16 B on its mbar_reduce
+                # (both pointers are local; store_async_dsmem maps them to the peer).
+                cute.arch.store_async_dsmem(
+                    sSlots4[(None, 0), (j, slot)].iterator,
+                    tuple(r4[i].bitcast(Int32) for i in range(4)),
+                    mbar_reduce,
+                    owner,
+                )
+        cute.arch.mbarrier_wait(mbar_reduce, 0)
+
+        # 3. Reduce and store my segment, 2 floats per thread per iteration.
+        rows_left = cute.size(mC_mnl, mode=[1]) - n_idx * self.cta_n
+        # ((2, 1), (cta_m / 2, cta_n)): expert pairs of this CTA's output tile. Built
+        # with local_tile so the compiler can prove each pair 8 B aligned (one
+        # st.global.v2 per pair); indexing mC with a hand-computed offset loses that
+        # and splits the store.
+        gC2 = cute.zipped_divide(
+            cute.local_tile(mC_mnl, (self.cta_m, self.cta_n), (e_idx, n_idx, 0)),
+            (2, 1),
+        )
+        n2 = SEG // 2
+        for it in cutlass.range_constexpr(
+            (n2 + _EPILOG_THREADS - 1) // _EPILOG_THREADS
+        ):
+            idx = it * _EPILOG_THREADS + epi_tid
+            if idx < n2:
+                flat = split_rank * SEG + 2 * idx
+                row = flat // RW
+                col = flat % RW
+                acc = cute.make_rmem_tensor((2,), Float32)
+                cute.autovec_copy(sStage2[(None, 0), (col // 2, row)], acc)
+                for p in cutlass.range_constexpr(S - 1):
+                    cute.autovec_copy(sSlots2[(None, 0), (idx, p)], r2)
+                    acc.store(acc.load() + r2.load())
+                if row < rows_left:
+                    cute.autovec_copy(acc, gC2[(None, 0), (col // 2, row)])

+def _smem_capacity(device=None) -> int:
+    """Shared memory per block of the current device."""
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device) == (10, 7):
+        # The device query does not report the sm_107 capacity; CuTe DSL's does.
+        return cutlass.memory.get_smem_capacity_in_bytes("sm_107")
+    return torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device).shared_memory_per_block_optin
+
+
+def _smem_bytes(tactic: RouterTactic, stages: int) -> int:
+    """Upper bound of the kernel's shared memory (allocation order and alignment)."""
+
+    def align(value: int, alignment: int) -> int:
+        return (value + alignment - 1) // alignment * alignment
+
+    # SharedStorage: ab pipeline (2 per stage), acc pipeline (2), mbar_reduce, TMEM slot.
+    cursor = (2 * stages + 3) * _MBARRIER_BYTES + 4
+    stage_bytes = tactic.cta_k * _FP32_BYTES * stages
+    cursor = align(cursor, _AB_BUFFER_ALIGN_BYTES) + tactic.mma_m * stage_bytes  # sA
+    cursor = align(cursor, _AB_BUFFER_ALIGN_BYTES) + tactic.mma_n * stage_bytes  # sB
+    tile = tactic.mma_m * tactic.mma_n
+    cursor = align(cursor, _MAILBOX_ALIGN_BYTES) + tile * _FP32_BYTES  # sStage
+    slots = (tactic.split_k - 1) * (tile // tactic.split_k) * _FP32_BYTES
+    return align(cursor, _MAILBOX_ALIGN_BYTES) + slots  # sSlots
+
+
+def _max_stages(
+    tactic: RouterTactic, smem_capacity: int, limit: int = _MAX_STAGES
+) -> int:
+    return next(
+        (
+            s
+            for s in range(limit, _MIN_STAGES - 1, -1)
+            if _smem_bytes(tactic, s) <= smem_capacity
+        ),
+        0,
+    )
+
+
+def default_tactic(
+    m: int,
+    e: int,
+    k: int,
+    split_k: int = 0,
+    mma_m: int = 64,
+    stages: int = 0,
+    cta_k: int = 64,
+    mma_n: int = 0,
+    pdl: bool = True,
+    smem_capacity: int | None = None,
+    max_stages_limit: int = _MAX_STAGES,
+) -> RouterTactic:
+    smem_capacity = smem_capacity or _smem_capacity()
+    # Token tile: the smallest covering M, or an explicit one (larger M runs
+    # several token tiles).
+    mma_n = mma_n or next((n for n in _MMA_N if n >= m), _MMA_N[-1])
+    # Largest split whose sStage + sSlots still leave room for 4 pipeline stages.
+    for split in (split_k,) if split_k else reversed(_SPLIT_K):
+        tactic = RouterTactic(mma_m, mma_n, split, _MIN_STAGES, cta_k, pdl)
+        max_stages = _max_stages(tactic, smem_capacity, max_stages_limit)
+        if max_stages >= (_MIN_STAGES if split_k else 4) and (k // cta_k) % split == 0:
+            break
+    tactic = dataclasses.replace(
+        tactic, ab_stages=min(stages, max_stages) if stages else max_stages
+    )
+    validate(tactic, m, e, k, smem_capacity)
+    return tactic
+
+
+def validate(
+    tactic: RouterTactic, m: int, e: int, k: int, smem_capacity: int | None = None
+) -> None:
+    """Reject a tactic that cannot serve ``x[m, k] @ w[e, k]^T``."""
+    smem_capacity = smem_capacity or _smem_capacity()
+    if tactic.mma_m not in _MMA_M or tactic.mma_n not in _MMA_N:
+        raise ValueError(f"unsupported tile {tactic}")
+    if tactic.split_k not in _SPLIT_K or tactic.cta_k not in _CTA_K:
+        raise ValueError(f"unsupported split_k / cta_k in {tactic}")
+    if m < 1 or e % tactic.mma_m:
+        raise ValueError(f"M={m}, E={e} do not fit {tactic}")
+    if k % tactic.cta_k or (k // tactic.cta_k) % tactic.split_k:
+        raise ValueError(f"K={k} does not split into {tactic.split_k} x {tactic.cta_k}")
+    if (
+        tactic.ab_stages < _MIN_STAGES
+        or _smem_bytes(tactic, tactic.ab_stages) > smem_capacity
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(f"tactic {tactic} does not fit in {smem_capacity} B of SMEM")
+    tile = tactic.mma_m * tactic.mma_n
+    if (tile // tactic.split_k) % 4:
+        raise ValueError(f"tile {tactic} gives a rank segment of partial 16 B pieces")
+

+def _cute_operands(x: torch.Tensor, w: torch.Tensor, out: torch.Tensor):
+    # W is fully static; x and out have a dynamic token count M.
+    return (
+        from_dlpack(w, assumed_align=16),
+        from_dlpack(x, assumed_align=16).mark_compact_shape_dynamic(
+            mode=0, stride_order=x.dim_order()
+        ),
+        from_dlpack(out, assumed_align=16).mark_compact_shape_dynamic(
+            mode=0, stride_order=out.dim_order()
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def _compile(tactic: RouterTactic, e: int, k: int, use_pdl: bool):
+    # One binary per tactic and router shape (E, K); it serves every M.
+    key = (tactic, e, k, use_pdl)
+    compiled = _COMPILE_CACHE.get(key)
+    if compiled is None:
+        x = torch.empty((tactic.mma_n, k), device="cuda")
+        w = torch.empty((e, k), device="cuda")
+        out = torch.empty((tactic.mma_n, e), device="cuda")
+        compiled = cute.compile(
+            RouterGemmKernel(tactic, use_pdl),
+            *_cute_operands(x, w, out),
+            cuda.CUstream(torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream),
+        )
+        _COMPILE_CACHE[key] = compiled
+    return compiled

+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    w: torch.Tensor,
+    out: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    tactic: RouterTactic | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``x[M, H]`` fp32 @ ``w[E, H]^T`` fp32 -> fp32 ``[M, E]`` (TF32 MMA, fp32 accumulate)."""

+    e, k = w.shape

+# replace one with register_serve_table().

+# slice -> gather + norm + NVFP4 quant on the main stream, router + top-8 routing on the side stream),
+# CUDA graph.
+#

+# 16-CTA cluster waits for SMs, which a standalone run does not show. M ranges where no tactic
+# beat cuBLAS at both TP sizes keep cuBLAS.
+#
+# A None entry keeps cuBLAS for its M range.
+_SM107_STAGES = 24
+_SERVE_TABLES = {
+    (10, 3): (
+        (16, dict(split_k=8, cta_k=128)),
+        (64, dict(split_k=4, cta_k=64, mma_n=32)),
+        (192, dict(split_k=8, cta_k=64, mma_n=64)),
+        (256, dict(split_k=4, cta_k=64, mma_n=32)),

+            dict(split_k=8, cta_k=32, mma_n=64, max_stages_limit=_SM107_STAGES),
+        ),
+        (
+            64,
+            dict(split_k=16, cta_k=128, mma_n=32, max_stages_limit=_SM107_STAGES),
+        ),
+        (
+            128,
+            dict(split_k=16, cta_k=32, mma_n=64, max_stages_limit=_SM107_STAGES),
+        ),
+        (256, None),
+        (
+            512,
+            dict(
+                split_k=4,
+                cta_k=32,
+                mma_m=128,
+                mma_n=64,
+                max_stages_limit=_SM107_STAGES,
+            ),
+        ),
+        (1024, None),
+    ),
+}
+SERVE_MAX_TOKENS = 1024
+
+
+def register_serve_table(capability: tuple[int, int], table) -> None:
+    """Add or replace the serving tactics of a compute capability: a sequence of
+    (max M, default_tactic overrides or None for cuBLAS) in increasing M, covering M
+    up to SERVE_MAX_TOKENS."""
+    _SERVE_TABLES[tuple(capability)] = tuple(table)
+    serve_tactic.cache_clear()
+
+
+@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def _capability(device_index: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    return torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device_index)
+
+
+def _serve_overrides(m: int, capability: tuple) -> dict | None:
+    for max_m, overrides in _SERVE_TABLES[capability]:
+        if m <= max_m:
+            return overrides
+    raise ValueError(f"M={m} is above the serving table of {capability}")
+
+
+@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def serve_tactic(
+    m: int, e: int, k: int, smem_capacity: int = 0, capability: tuple = (10, 3)
+) -> RouterTactic:
+    smem_capacity = smem_capacity or _smem_capacity()
+    overrides = _serve_overrides(m, capability)
+    if overrides is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"M={m} runs cuBLAS on {capability}")
+    return default_tactic(m, e, k, smem_capacity=smem_capacity, **overrides)
+
+
+def router_tf32_eligible(x: torch.Tensor, w: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
+    """FP32 router logits for 2 <= M <= SERVE_MAX_TOKENS on a device with a serving
+    table (M = 1 keeps the GEMV), only with TF32 matmuls allowed: under "highest"
+    cuBLAS keeps the logits FP32."""
+    return (
+        x.is_cuda
+        and torch.get_float32_matmul_precision() != "highest"
+        and x.dim() == 2
+        and 2 <= x.shape[0] <= SERVE_MAX_TOKENS
+        and _capability(x.device.index) in _SERVE_TABLES
+        and _serve_overrides(x.shape[0], _capability(x.device.index)) is not None
+        and x.dtype == torch.float32
+        and w.dtype == torch.float32
+        and x.shape[1] == w.shape[1]
+        and x.shape[1] % 128 == 0
+        and w.shape[0] % 128 == 0
+        and x.is_contiguous()
+        and w.is_contiguous()
+        and x.data_ptr() % 32 == 0
+        and w.data_ptr() % 32 == 0
+    )
+
+
+def router_tf32(
+    x: torch.Tensor, w: torch.Tensor, tactic: RouterTactic | None = None
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Router logits with the device's serving tactic, or an explicit one."""
+    return router_logits_tf32(x, w, tactic=tactic)

+)

+# FlashInfer's NvFP4 x NvFP4 tile candidates; sync with selectDefaultTileN.

+# trtllm_moe_max_da_multi_tile_tokens(num_experts), 2048 at 256 experts.
+_MAX_SPLIT_TOKENS = 1024

+_MAX_SPLIT_TILE = 128

+
+def _default_tile(*, num_tokens: int, top_k: int, num_local_experts: int) -> int:
+    """The tile FlashInfer picks without a tuned tactic: one below the tile covering tokens per expert."""
+    per_expert = num_tokens * top_k / num_local_experts
+    i = next(
+        (k for k, t in enumerate(_FP4_TILES) if t >= per_expert), len(_FP4_TILES) - 1
+    )
+    return _FP4_TILES[max(i - 1, 0)]

+    ((10, 3), 4): 512,
+    ((10, 3), 8): 512,
+    ((10, 7), 4): 8,
+    ((10, 7), 8): 8,

+
+
+def split_enabled(

+

+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _tf32_matmuls():
+    # The server allows TF32 matmuls; the kernel is only eligible then.
+    previous = torch.get_float32_matmul_precision()
+    torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("high")
+    yield
+    torch.set_float32_matmul_precision(previous)

+    ],
+)
+def test_explicit_tactics_match_fp64(m: int, overrides: dict):

+
+

+"""Muse Spark routed MoE split: metadata + body must match the ordinary FlashInfer call bitwise."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=120, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+
+if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] != 10:
+    pytest.skip("SM10x required", allow_module_level=True)
+
+from flashinfer.fused_moe import (  # noqa: E402
+    QuantConfig,
+    QuantFormat,
+    TrtllmFp4Config,
+    trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe,
+)
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.muse_spark.routed_moe_split import (  # noqa: E402
+    get_routed_moe_split,
+    split_enabled,
+    split_supported,
+)
+
+# Muse Spark experts: 256 routed experts, top-8, hidden 4096.
+H, I, E, TOP_K = 4096, 4096, 256, 8
+# (local experts, M): 64 / 32 local experts are TP4 / TP8 with EP; tiles 8 to 128.
+SPLIT_CASES = [(64, m) for m in (1, 16, 128, 512, 1024)] + [
+    (32, m) for m in (1, 16, 128, 512, 768)
+]
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def weights():
+    quant = QuantConfig(weight=QuantFormat.NVFP4, activation=QuantFormat.NVFP4)
+    views = {}
+    for local in (64, 32):
+        torch.manual_seed(local)
+        w1 = (torch.randn(local, 2 * I, H, device="cuda") * 0.02).to(torch.bfloat16)
+        w2 = (torch.randn(local, H, I, device="cuda") * 0.02).to(torch.bfloat16)
+        views[local] = TrtllmFp4Config.prepare_weights(
+            w1,
+            w2,
+            quant=quant,
+            num_local_experts=local,
+            hidden_size=H,
+            intermediate_size=I,
+            device=torch.device("cuda"),
+        )
+        del w1, w2
+    yield quant, views
+    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
+
+
+def _inputs(quant, m: int, seed: int, per_token: bool):
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    x = torch.randn(m, H, device="cuda", generator=g) * 2
+    hs, sf = TrtllmFp4Config.prepare_activations(x.to(torch.bfloat16), quant=quant)
+    ids = torch.stack(
+        [torch.randperm(E, device="cuda", generator=g)[:TOP_K] for _ in range(m)]
+    ).to(torch.int32)
+    w = torch.rand(m, TOP_K, device="cuda", generator=g).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    packed = (ids << 16) | (w.view(torch.int16).to(torch.int32) & 0xFFFF)
+    scale = torch.rand(m, device="cuda", generator=g) + 0.5 if per_token else None
+    return hs, sf, packed, scale
+
+
+def _kwargs(view, local, hs, sf, packed, scale):
+    return dict(
+        topk_ids=packed,
+        routing_bias=None,
+        hidden_states=hs,
+        hidden_states_scale=sf,
+        gemm1_weights=view["gemm1_weights"],
+        gemm1_weights_scale=view["gemm1_weights_scale"],
+        gemm1_bias=None,
+        gemm1_alpha=view.get("gemm1_alpha"),
+        gemm1_beta=None,
+        gemm1_clamp_limit=None,
+        gemm2_weights=view["gemm2_weights"],
+        gemm2_weights_scale=view["gemm2_weights_scale"],
+        gemm2_bias=None,
+        output1_scale_scalar=view.get("output1_scale_scalar"),
+        output1_scale_gate_scalar=view.get("output1_scale_gate_scalar"),
+        output2_scale_scalar=view.get("output2_scale_scalar"),
+        per_token_scale=scale,
+        num_experts=E,
+        top_k=TOP_K,
+        n_group=0,
+        topk_group=0,
+        intermediate_size=I,
+        local_expert_offset=local,
+        local_num_experts=local,
+        routed_scaling_factor=1.0,
+        routing_method_type=1,
+        do_finalize=False,
+        activation_type=3,
+    )
+
+
+def _finalize(m, gemm2_out, expert_weights, expanded_idx_to_permuted_idx):
+    """Per-token weighted sum in top-k order; padded FC2 rows are not compared."""
+    idx = expanded_idx_to_permuted_idx.long().view(m, TOP_K)
+    # Padded slots (-1) may hold uninitialized FC2 rows and expert weights (NaN * 0 is NaN);
+    # zero their products explicitly.
+    rows = gemm2_out.float()[idx.clamp(min=0)] * expert_weights.float().view(
+        m, TOP_K, 1
+    )
+    return torch.where((idx >= 0).view(m, TOP_K, 1), rows, 0.0).sum(dim=1)
+
+
+def _ordinary(kwargs, m):
+    return _finalize(m, *trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe(**kwargs)[:3])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("per_token", [False, True], ids=["static", "per_token"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("local, m", SPLIT_CASES)
+def test_split_matches_ordinary_call(weights, local, m, per_token):
+    """Populate on a side stream and join before the body, as serving does; then replay a graph
+    of the same sequence with new routing and activations copied into its inputs."""
+    assert split_supported(num_tokens=m, top_k=TOP_K, num_local_experts=local)
+    quant, views = weights
+    hs, sf, packed, scale = _inputs(quant, m, seed=m, per_token=per_token)
+    kwargs = _kwargs(views[local], local, hs, sf, packed, scale)
+    split = get_routed_moe_split(
+        packed, num_experts=E, local_expert_offset=local, num_local_experts=local
+    )
+    side = torch.cuda.Stream()
+
+    def run():
+        main = torch.cuda.current_stream()
+        side.wait_stream(main)
+        with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+            split.populate(packed)
+        main.wait_stream(side)
+        return split.run_body(**kwargs)
+
+    assert torch.equal(_finalize(m, *run()), _ordinary(kwargs, m)), "eager"
+
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        captured = run()
+    for seed in (m + 1, m + 2):
+        new_hs, new_sf, new_packed, new_scale = _inputs(quant, m, seed, per_token)
+        hs.copy_(new_hs)
+        sf.copy_(new_sf)
+        packed.copy_(new_packed)
+        if per_token:
+            scale.copy_(new_scale)
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.equal(_finalize(m, *captured), _ordinary(kwargs, m)), (
+            f"replay seed={seed}"
+        )
+
+
+def test_split_gate():
+    """The gate admits the tiles measured bitwise (<= 128) and keeps the rest on the ordinary call."""
+    for local, m in SPLIT_CASES:
+        assert split_supported(num_tokens=m, top_k=TOP_K, num_local_experts=local)
+    # Tile 192 at 32 local experts, and above the measured token range.
+    assert not split_supported(num_tokens=960, top_k=TOP_K, num_local_experts=32)
+    assert not split_supported(num_tokens=1025, top_k=TOP_K, num_local_experts=64)
+
+
+def test_split_enabled_per_gpu_and_tp():
+    """Only measured (GPU, TP) pairs take the split, from their measured token count."""
+    for tp in (4, 8):
+        assert split_enabled(num_tokens=8, tp_size=tp, capability=(10, 7))
+        assert split_enabled(num_tokens=1024, tp_size=tp, capability=(10, 7))
+        assert not split_enabled(num_tokens=256, tp_size=tp, capability=(10, 3))
+        assert split_enabled(num_tokens=512, tp_size=tp, capability=(10, 3))
+    assert not split_enabled(num_tokens=4, tp_size=4, capability=(10, 7))
+    assert not split_enabled(num_tokens=64, tp_size=2, capability=(10, 7))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    import sys
+
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))

+"""Muse Spark router logits on SM10x: TF32 tcgen05 GEMM with a cluster split-K.
+
+Computes ``logits[M, E] = x[M, H] @ W[E, H]^T`` (fp32 in, fp32 accumulate, fp32 out)
+in one launch; cuBLAS's TF32 path runs a split-K GEMM plus a separate reduce kernel.
+
+Both operands are TMA-loaded through a TF32 tensor map,
+so the copy engine rounds them fp32 -> TF32 (round to nearest even) on the way into
+shared memory: the MMA sees exactly the operands of a round-to-nearest TF32 GEMM,
+and the weight is used as stored.
+
+The problem is swapped so the experts fill the MMA M dimension and the few tokens
+sit in N. In kernel coordinates:
+  A:  (E, K, L)  K-major  -- router weight
+  B:  (M, K, L)  K-major  -- activations
+  C:  (E, M, L)  E-major  -- view of the row-major [M, E] logits
+E and K are static (one compile per router shape); M is dynamic; L = 1.
+
+## Grid and clusters
+  grid    = (E / cta_m, token_tiles * split_k, 1), cluster = (1, split_k, 1)
+  The ``split_k`` CTAs of a cluster share one (cta_m, cta_n) output tile and each
+  accumulates an equal, contiguous K slice; the epilogue reduces the slices over
+  DSMEM. Larger M runs several token tiles (grid-y = token tile * split_k + rank).
+  There is no TMA multicast: each CTA loads its own K slice.
+
+## Warp specialization (8 warps, 256 threads/CTA)
+  Warps 0-3  EPILOG  TMEM alloc/free; TMEM -> RMEM, split-K reduce-scatter over
+                     DSMEM, st.global
+  Warp 4     MMA     tcgen05.mma into TMEM; releases each stage (tcgen05.commit)
+  Warp 5     LOAD_W  TMA-loads weight tiles into sA[..., stage]; with PDL it does
+                     not wait for the previous kernel and launches the dependent
+                     grid once its loads are issued
+  Warp 6     LOAD_X  griddepcontrol.wait (PDL), then TMA-loads activation tiles
+                     into sB[..., stage]
+  Warp 7     idle

+  full[stage]       2 arrivals (LOAD_W + LOAD_X arrive_and_expect_tx) + TMA bytes
+  empty[stage]      1 arrival (MMA tcgen05.commit)
+  acc pipeline      PipelineUmmaAsync, 1 stage: MMA -> EPILOG ("accumulator ready")

+  mbar_reduce       1 arrival (EPILOG thread 0 arrive_and_expect_tx) + the

+  All mbarriers are initialized before the cluster arrive/wait, so no peer can
